acts.desc: Ira Glass speaks with Charles Salter, the original Georgia Rambler, about his column from the 1970s.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: David Kestenbaum finds that the most unforgettable person in this county is a dead guy. A guy named Franklin Delano Roosevelt. Who had some secrets in Meriweather. David's with Planet Money, a collaboration between NPR News and This American Life.
acts.title: Meriwether County

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Comedian Eugene Mirman meets three friends all named Matt who claim they are the most unforgettable people in this county: Quiet Matt, Big Matt and Artist Matt.
acts.title: Hall County

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Allen Wigington, former Chief Deputy at the Pickens County Sheriff's department, now magistrate judge, tells the story a soldier killed in Iraq—Specialist David Collins—arriving back home in Georgia to be buried.
acts.title: Pickens County

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Producer Lisa Pollak learns some of the things people in Chattooga are talking about, thanks to a Summerville News column called "Soundoff."
acts.title: Chattooga County

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: Producer Jane Feltes speaks with Adam Vickers, one of the owners of Vickers Music in the town of Douglas.
acts.title: Coffee County and Bacon County

acts.label: Act Six
acts.desc: Sarah Koenig drives to Jeffersonville, a town of about 1200, and when she asks who is the most interesting person in town, she's led to Sonya Mallory.
acts.title: Twiggs County

acts.label: Act Seven
acts.desc: Chuck Salter, son of Georgia Rambler Charles Salter, Sr., visits a man named Windell Cleveland, who was interviewed by his father 33 years ago. Chuck is a senior writer at Fast Company Magazine.
acts.title: Elbert County
